column1: # flow_ref 1 source=tests/spec/flow_semantics/event_reset_values.onsa tests=21 evaluated=21 unavailable=0 skipped=0 waiting=0
@ a flow of sample reset by an event starts again at the frame of the event, and the frame gives its own input: the same in every way of writing it
@ reset_if~ with an event does not touch sample_tick(): the time goes on
@ the last event inside the part is T.default() after the reset: the reset is before the stage where the part gives its own event
@ a field of sample / 2 is T.default() after the reset until the next tick, and the counter inside starts again from its init
@ the reset goes down to the instances inside: a running sum of a running sum, and a sum of events made inside
@ two calls of one flow keep their own state, and two producers that give an event at one frame reset each its call
@ an event part: a reset by an event that a line above gave comes before the add, one from the argument or from a line above the input comes after it
@ two sources: the one written first ticks first, so the reset is after the add when the input is written first and before it when the condition is
@ the producer of sample / 4 ticks before the producers of sample of the same frame, whatever the order of the lines
@ a delay of a value of sample is put back to its init at the frame of the event, and that frame gives the init
@ one event given to two inputs: the input declared first ticks first, and what its tick gives is done before the next input ticks
@ reset_if~ twice on an event: each condition resets the whole, the frame where both hold is one reset
@ a condition of the kind block or a constant next to an event: true resets at each frame, false does nothing
process 0 params k=true frames=3 in x=[1 2 3]
process 0 params k=false frames=3 in x=[4 5 2]
@ prev~ of an event reset by the same event: the delay is at its init for that event, and T.default() is the value before the first event
@ delay~ and vdelay~ of an event reset by the event: the line of the stored events is back to the init with its write place
@ a loop of an event delay is reset to its init: the sum of the events before, where a reset sends it to 0 again
@ a delay of an event with a condition of the kind block: true resets at each tick of the event, so each tick gives the init; false does nothing
process 0 params k=false frames=6 in x=[0 0 5 0 3 0]
process 1 params k=true frames=6 in x=[0 0 5 0 3 0]
@ a receiver written above its producer gets its event through ^ after its own stage, so the output of a frame is the sum before it, and an event written above it resets before the read
@ a call with a reset in the first argument of a delay reads the event where it is written: the last value before the producer of that event ticks again
@ the last event of a condition is T.default() before the first event: a condition on its value holds until the event comes
@ a run in pieces, with a call of 0 frames and a reset of the state, is the run in one call
